A1.justification: Both complete PDFs describe TigerLLM and its two datasets. Text, tables, figures and appendices are readable, and v2's appendix material can be matched to its relocated presentation in v3.

before.justification: v2 reports original TigerLLM benchmark results in Table 2 and training-loss curves in Appendix C.

after.justification: v3 retains the original benchmark results and training-loss curves and additionally reports a filtering acceptance rate.

M1.justification: v3's Response Drafting step adds a rule selecting the highest-scoring draft using coherence metric c(i,r); v2 describes generating a candidate response followed by filtering. This is a limited addition to the described procedure; teacher models, model architectures and overall training stages remain unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions retain the textbook corpus, Bangla-Instruct, the ten seed-task categories and all six evaluation benchmarks. The added HumanEval discussion explains the existing use of mHumanEval-bn rather than introducing another evaluated task.

E2.justification: Table 2 retains the same ten comparator rows and model sizes. Newly discussed models such as BLOOM, AYA and GPT2-Bangla are not added to the reported evaluation.

E3.justification: The benchmark settings, Pass@1 reporting and all hyperparameter values in Tables 3–5 are unchanged. Hardware and training-duration descriptions move into Section 5. The new dataset-composition statement does not establish a changed sampling or evaluation design.

E4.justification: No ablation, robustness test, sensitivity analysis or error study is added or removed. Figures 3–4 contain identical training-loss plots, relocated from Appendix C into the main text.

E5.justification: Both versions report seed 42 in Tables 4–5 and provide no new repeated-run counts, confidence intervals or significance tests. The newly stated average filtering acceptance rate introduces no accompanying uncertainty-estimation procedure.

E6.justification: v3 newly reports that approximately 63% of generated pairs pass filtering and describes accepted pairs as 40% basic, 40% intermediate and 20% advanced; v2 reports those complexity proportions only for seed tasks. Every Table 2 score and both training-loss curves remain unchanged.

T1.justification: Appendix A.3 retains the same filtering definitions, thresholds and conjunctive acceptance rule. The coherence metric and task-dependent minimum-length notation referenced in v3 already appear in v2's appendix; no theorem, proof or substantive mathematical derivation is added.

C1.justification: The abstract, contributions and conclusion retain the same claims about the two datasets, 1B/9B TigerLLM models, superiority over alternatives and 30–55% performance improvements. Rewording does not change their scientific scope.

C2.justification: Both versions attribute performance to curated educational text and high-quality instruction data. They retain the same limitations concerning textbook-domain coverage, corpus size, instruction diversity and model scale; the revised pipeline explanation preserves the existing quality-control interpretation.

D1.justification: v3 omits v2's explicit statement that seed demonstrations are sampled uniformly at random and removes the Lambda Labs provider identification and link. Hardware specifications, training times, hyperparameter tables and repository access information otherwise remain, with setup details relocated.

R1.justification: The new Section 2 substantially broadens positioning through Bangla encoders, multilingual decoders, cross-lingual performance gaps and GPT2-Bangla, adding works including BERT, BANGLA BERT, BLOOM, AYA and Jin et al. References to bnTenTen and the original LLaMA paper are removed; mHumanEval and MojoBench publication updates concern retained works.

P1.justification: v3 adds a dedicated Related Work section, rewrites the four instruction-generation steps and integrates Appendix C and Appendix B.1 into an expanded main-text TigerLLM section. This substantially reorganizes the narrative, alongside smaller edits to future work, author information and reference formatting.

P2.justification: Figures 2–4 move from Appendix C into the main method section, while Figure 2 receives new TigerLLM logos. Wider columns, resized figures and tables, revised author blocks and redistributed table spacing produce extensive layout changes without changing the benchmark entries or loss plots.

improvement.justification: Broader research context and integration of the previously scattered training explanation, hardware details and figures make v3 easier to follow; the filtering acceptance rate adds modest transparency. These gains are limited by lost sampling specificity and a new inconsistency: Section 2 describes titu-Gemma as instruction-tuned, while Table 1 still lists no finetuning.
